one_line: Freshly graded rectangular pad (~90 x 60 m) built against an existing track with a new spur, Aug-Sep 2023, Salar de Arizaro margin: earthworks, likely exploration pad.
summary: before.png (Sentinel-2 median May-Jul 2023) and hires.png (Esri, WorldView-3, 2023-07-21, one day before the last-absent date) show only a faint NNE-SSW vehicle track crossing the footprint box on uniform bare alluvial-fan ground; after.png (Nov 2023-Feb 2024) shows a crisp, straight-edged pale rectangle sitting directly against the west side of that track, the track itself brighter and wider, and a new straight spur leaving the junction westward to a small bright patch about 400-700 m away. difference.png shows the rectangle and the three straight lines converging on it as the strongest brightenings in the 2 km panel, with the NDVI panel flat; falsecolor_after.png shows the pad pale in SWIR1/NIR/red, i.e. dry exposed light subsoil, not water or vegetation. The brief's shape metrics (4 corners, rectangularity 0.87, 104 x 62 m, orientation 0 deg), the clean single step in timeseries.png (inside ~0.05 above the ring in every scene from 2023-09-27 through mid-2025; NBR -0.10 to +0.08-0.11), Landsat confirmation and a SAR contrast drop of 0.83 dB (smoother surface) all fit a bladed platform. All three sceptics (human activity, natural processes, data artefacts) refuted the candidate with high confidence and the panel agrees: this is ordinary earthworks, a graded pad with an access track, of the kind common for lithium-brine exploration on the Salar de Arizaro margin (a sibling pad, SW-B19-PUNA-OC0014, appeared 3.7 km north in the same period). The specific operator and purpose are inferred, not seen; the earthworks themselves are seen.
explanation: Human earthworks: a graded rectangular platform (about 90 x 60 m) bladed on the west side of pre-existing OSM track 399502073, with the track re-graded and a new westward spur track cut to a short-lived second worksite, between 2023-07-22 and 2023-09-27. Scraping the darker desert pavement exposed pale fine subsoil (visible/NIR/SWIR1 brightening, NDVI and NDWI unchanged). Most likely a mineral-exploration (lithium brine) drill or camp pad on the eastern margin of Salar de Arizaro.
next_step: Any sub-metre image of -25.0977, -67.6248 acquired after September 2023 (Maxar, Airbus, Planet SkySat, or an Esri/Google mosaic refresh; the Esri Wayback record still ends at the 2023-07-21 picture here) to show blade/berm edges, tyre marks, a drill collar or camp equipment on the pad; or the Salta provincial mining cadastre / environmental-impact register for a 2023 exploration permit covering this part of the Arizaro margin, naming the operator.
